In the function void date2gal(const datetime_t *t, galtime_t *g), which is a copy of date2gps in GPS-SDR-SIM, the calculation is wrong. According to GST (Galileo System Time), the start epoch is 00:00 UT on Sunday 22nd August 1999 (midnight between 21st and 22nd August). In the code the start epoch is midnight between Jan 5 and Jan 6 in 1980. This difference may cause to wrong time transmission in the nav messages (leading the receiver to sense a wrong UTC time).
https://www.gsc-europa.eu/galileoSystemTime
title: date2gal

body:
First of all, thanks for this great project.
It seems, there are few bugs concerning the generation of the I/NAV data message though...
1) CRC seems to be wrong
a) There is one obvious bug when the offset is not incremented after the Even/Odd and Page Type bits are inserted to the middle of the page. CRC field is then 2 bits early.
b) The CRC computation algorimth is probably wrong. E.g., BitStream is handled like an array of nav message bytes, but each field is filled with a single bit. Also important to note that the GNSS usage of the CRC24Q usually includes the message lengths which are non-integer multiplies of the full bytes (i.e. there are some leftover bits which need a special care after the last full byte). Also when you want to get the correct signature, it seems that you need to let the algorithm process the crc result register three more times with the zero input byte (size of the CRC signature).

2) There is a bug in generation of I/NAV Word Type 5 ... there should be 23 spare bits at the end, not 3. This causes the rest of the message including the CRC field shifted 20 bits to the left.

3) There is probably still something else fishy somewhere since both ublox and GSRx show the position several meters to several tens of meters off.
title: INAV message generation issues
